page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose compute instance built on AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The platform exposes 96 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, operating with one thread per core and completely bypassing hypervisor virtualization layers. Memory configuration comprises 384 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM, offering a standardized 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per physical core. Per-core caching includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, backed by a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Networking capabilities provide a high-throughput 200 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring external block or object storage for persistent data requirements.

Synthetic and application benchmarks demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance and high memory bandwidth. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the 96 dedicated Neoverse-V2 cores achieve top-tier output, complemented by top-tier bzip3 multi-threaded decompression throughput of 827.29 GB/s. DDR5 memory throughput reaches 434.56 GB/s for uncached reads and 245.92 GB/s for uncached writes, driving top-tier throughput in memory-sensitive operational tests. The instance recorded 195.1 million Redis SET operations per second and 187.68 GB/s in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference achieves top-tier generation rates on 7B parameter models at 49.13 tokens per second and strong performance on 70B models at 5.6 tokens per second, though single-core compute tasks and small-model prompt processing place in the average performance tier.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated core implementation eliminates multi-tenant resource contention and hypervisor jitter, translating into predictable multi-tenant consolidation and thread execution. While the lack of onboard NVMe drives necessitates external network storage orchestration and single-threaded performance remains average, the combination of 96 physical cores, massive memory bandwidth, and 200 Gbps networking yields strong throughput density for parallelized execution. The m8gb.metal-24xl is appropriate for large-scale distributed caching, high-concurrency web serving, parallel batch computation, in-memory data processing, and microservice container fleets.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores running on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture at 2.8 GHz. Equipped with 384 GB of DDR5 system memory configured at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core, this instance provides direct hardware access without hypervisor virtualization overhead. Network connectivity is supported by a 200 Gbps baseline interface, though the system includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures. In benchmark testing, the platform demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute throughput, high DDR5 uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 434 GB/s read, and strong static web serving capacity alongside 195.1 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread processing falls into average ranges, the dedicated physical core layout achieves massive parallel scaling and memory efficiency. The m8gb.metal-24xl is suited for high-density containerized workloads, in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing, and large-scale web microservices.
